turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How may I help you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm here because um I've been having some pain in my left knee for the past two months and it's not getting better. It feels stiff and um I just haven't been able to uh, you know, use it as well, as well as I was using it before um and it's just limited some of my daily activities.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, and where, uh so it's, the pain is in your left knee. Where are you feeling this pain specifically? Is it at the front of the knee, the sides, or or the the back? Could you point to it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It feels like it's mostly on the front.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Like deep within that um kneecap.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and you said the pain started two months ago?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, well, it's always been a little like tender. Um but now it's more painful.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And so, so has it been getting worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say so, slowly getting worse.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uh and when you get uh pain in the left knee, how long does it typically last for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It usually hurts while I'm doing, while I'm moving it, or just after, but if I if I rest, the pain eventually goes away. Um but when I first wake up in the morning, that joint feels stiff. And then when I start using it, using it more, it's less stiff, but it becomes painful.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so you have some stiffness in the morning?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how long does it last for? Like 30 minutes, 60 minutes or or longer?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: The stiffness or pain?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, the the stiffness.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh the stiffness goes away in like yeah 15 to 30 minutes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how would you describe the pain, um in terms of its character?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It feels, it feels uh, I guess most of the time it's like it's like a dull kind of pain, but it can be sharp.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is there anything that makes the pain worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just with a lot of activity it gets worse.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And you feel it radiate anywhere else?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how would you describe the severity of your pain on a scale of 10 being the worst pain you've ever felt, and 1 being kind of very minimal pain.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I would give it maybe uh 7.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you had any injuries to your knee before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I can think of.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK. Um and have you been having any uh any weight loss recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, weight gain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Weight gain, OK. How much weight have you gained over the last uh several months?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Over the past six months, I'd say I've gained about 20 pounds.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had changes in your diet and or exercise?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I guess I've been eating a little bit more, um but no changes in exercise.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um have you been having any fevers or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about any night sweats?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no night sweats.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um have you had any changes to your vision or hearing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you had any changes to your uh sense of smell or sense of taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had a runny nose or or a sore throat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you had a cough or or any shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about any uh wheezing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No wheezing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, any chest pain or heart palpitations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright have you had any lightheadedness or dizziness?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and any confusion or memory loss?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and have you had any changes in appetite, like a loss of appetite?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, I, if anything, had a gain in appetite.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, uh have you had any nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about any abdominal pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. Um and how about any urinary problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no urinary problems.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um any changes to your bowel habits, like diarrhea or blood in the stool?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and have you had any rashes or skin changes or changes to your hair or nails?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any other joint pains? Or have you or do you have any joint swelling?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh I have some joint um swelling. It's it's not very visible, but it's it appears slightly more swollen than my left, sorry, than my right knee.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So just a little bit of swelling in your left knee, but no other joints?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um and have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I have um diabetes, high blood pressure and high cholesterol. And I'm overweight.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you take any medications for any of those conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm on insulin for diabetes. Um I'm on Ramipril for high blood pressure and I'm also on a statin for the cholesterol.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you have any allergies to medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and uh, have you had any surgeries in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and um are your immunizations up to date?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, uh, and could you tell me a little bit about your living situation currently, like like who you're living with and whereabouts?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I live with my husband in a house downtown.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um and are you working currently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I retired early.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I'll have a glass of wine every night.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so about 7 drinks per week?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and um, do you smoke cigarettes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, I don't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, how about the use of any recreational drugs like cannabis or uh or anything else?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. Um and is there any, uh, like musculoskeletal or like autoimmune conditions that run in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm no musculoskeletal issues uh that, I know diabetes runs in the family.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um alright, so that was everything I wanted to ask on history. So next I just wanted to do a physical exam, and just looking at the left knee, are you seeing any um swelling or redness uh on the knee?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um it appears slightly more swollen than my right knee.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, but are you seeing any redness?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No redness.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are there any temperature changes? Like does the knee feel hot or or warm?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and if you um press along the uh joint line, do you feel any pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm yeah, it feels a little tender.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And how about pain over any of the muscles, like the thigh muscles or the hamstrings or the calf muscles?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, those are fine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and then how about any pain over the patella or kneecap?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That that's a little bit more painful.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you able to bend your knee uh like like flex it, straighten it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh I can do that, it's just painful when I do that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um and uh and then how about walking, are you um, do you have an antalgic gait or or or a limp?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm no, no, well, I guess I'm I'm putting more weight on my right knee so it might appear to some people that I do have a slight limp.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any issues with moving your hip or your ankle?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um so I think that was everything I wanted to ask and check today. Did did you have any questions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um yeah, so um how do you, how can I treat my knee?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, certainly, so it it sounds like um this could be most likely osteoarthritis um of the left knee, which uh is something that would be best treated with uh trying to stay as active as you can, but but also pacing your activities as well, so that you're not um doing so much that the next day you're in significant amount of pain, but it's important to remember that um activity will help um with keeping your knee mobile, but also um actually help with reducing pain as well, and then also uh you could use Tylenol um as a medication for it. I wouldn't recommend ibuprofen or NSAIDs on a long term basis, although you could take those if you're having like an acute flare up of your pain. Um and then also like topical agents such as um like Voltaren or something like that you could put on your knee and um if it's really bad and it keeps um continuing on, we can consider something like a steroid injection as well.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, yeah, that sounds good. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, thank you.
